analysis:
The supplied files are test-only changes. FeatureWaitlistTests.swift is new and SandboxSetupTests.swift is modified, so there is no production-source change to evaluate. I found no concrete security regression in these units. The tests document the intended behaviour of the waitlist client and the sandbox-setup gate, which are implemented in production files outside this batch.

The tests assert these controls:
- Only https coordinators or loopback hosts receive the bearer token (FeatureWaitlistTests.swift lines 187-196). The same token is sent only on waitlist requests with an Authorization header (lines 198-221).
- Coordinator-supplied title, summary, start_command and error text are sanitized before terminal output. C0, C1, OSC and bidi characters and line separators become U+FFFD, and --json output is escaped (lines 298-321, 346-364).
- The join posts an empty `{}` body.
- A 404 from the waitlist lets sandbox setup go on (lines 555-573), while a waitlisted or revoked status stops setup before the Mac check or any download (lines 575-604). This relates to TB-013 and T-061, since setup downloads and runs an installer as the Mac's owner.
- A 403 on the gate is treated as refused, so setup does not continue.

The 404 fail-open behaviour is a deliberate, tested design choice. It is a product gate, not a security boundary, because installer integrity is covered separately under T-061.

The SandboxSetupTests.swift edits only add `waitlist: .approved` to existing SandboxSetupFlow call sites, which keeps those tests off the network.

The tests use hard-coded fake tokens and .invalid hosts, so they leak no real secrets.

Remaining integration questions:
- The production FeatureWaitlistClient, FeatureWaitlistView and SandboxSetupFlow gate are not in this batch. I could not verify that they actually enforce the token-scope, sanitization and redirect behaviour the tests assert.
- A redirect-following check is not asserted in these tests. It could not be confirmed from the evidence, so I recorded it as a question rather than a finding.
- Whether the production sandbox-setup gate treats a waitlist 404 or a transport failure as fail-open or fail-closed beyond what the tests show is also unverified.
